Title: [Bug] Gemini embeddings API returns 404, causes infinite retry loop and 100% CPU
Creator: dnaik-infinera
Body:
# Letta Server Bug Report: Gemini Embeddings Endpoint 404 Error

## Summary
Letta server v0.13.0 enters an infinite retry loop when `GEMINI_API_KEY` is set, causing 100% CPU usage due to incorrect Gemini API endpoint URL.

## Environment
- **Letta Version**: 0.13.0
- **Deployment**: Docker (letta/letta:latest)
- **OS**: Linux
- **Container**: letta-server
- **Date Observed**: November 6, 2025

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Set `GEMINI_API_KEY` environment variable in docker-compose.yml:
   ```yaml
   environment:
     - GEMINI_API_KEY=AIzaSy...
   ```
2. Start letta-server container
3. Observe server logs and CPU usage

## Expected Behavior
- Letta server should successfully call Gemini embeddings API using the correct endpoint
- CPU usage should remain normal (~1-5%)
- Embeddings requests should complete successfully

## Actual Behavior
- Server enters infinite retry loop attempting to call embeddings API
- CPU usage spikes to 100%+ and stays there
- Logs show continuous 404 errors:
  ```
  httpx - INFO - HTTP Request: POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/embeddings "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found"
  openai._base_client - INFO - Retrying request to /embeddings in 0.4XX seconds
  ```

## Root Cause
Letta is using an **incorrect endpoint URL** for Gemini embeddings:

**Current (incorrect):**
```
https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/embeddings
```

**Correct endpoint should be:**
```
https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{model}:embedContent
```

Or for the latest stable API:
```
https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1/models/{model}:embedContent
```

Example with specific model:
```
https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1/models/text-embedding-004:embedContent
```

## Impact
- **Critical**: Server becomes unusable with 100% CPU
- Users cannot use Gemini for embeddings
- Forces users to disable GEMINI_API_KEY or use alternative providers

## Logs
```
letta-server  | openai._base_client - INFO - Retrying request to /embeddings in 0.383874 seconds
letta-server  | openai._base_client - INFO - Retrying request to /embeddings in 0.482700 seconds
letta-server  | httpx - INFO - HTTP Request: POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/embeddings "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found"
letta-server  | httpx - INFO - HTTP Request: POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/embeddings "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found"
[...repeats infinitely...]
```

## Configuration Details
**docker-compose.yml environment:**
```yaml
environment:
  - LETTA_SERVER_PASS=${LETTA_SERVER_PASS:-}
  - LETTA_PG_URI=${LETTA_PG_URI:-postgresql://letta:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-letta}@postgres:5432/letta}
  - DATABASE_URL=${LETTA_PG_URI:-postgresql://letta:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-letta}@postgres:5432/letta}
  - GEMINI_API_KEY=${GEMINI_API_KEY:-}
```

**Server startup logs (successful):**
```
[[ Letta server // v0.13.0 ]]
▶ Server running at: http://0.0.0.0:8283
INFO: Started server process [1]
INFO: Application startup complete.
```

## Workaround
**Temporary fix**: Remove or disable GEMINI_API_KEY until this is resolved:
```bash
# In .env file
GEMINI_API_KEY=
```

Then restart letta-server:
```bash
docker compose restart letta-server
```

## Suggested Fix
Update the Gemini embeddings client code to use the correct endpoint:

1. Use the correct base URL with API version:
   - `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1/models/`

2. Append the model name and action:
   - Default model: `text-embedding-004`
   - Action: `:embedContent`

3. Full endpoint example:
   ```
   POST https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1/models/text-embedding-004:embedContent
   Header: x-goog-api-key: {GEMINI_API_KEY}
   ```

## References
- Google AI Gemini API Docs: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/embeddings
- Gemini Embeddings Endpoint: https://ai.google.dev/api/embeddings

## Additional Context
- OpenAI embeddings work fine as an alternative
- Issue does not occur when GEMINI_API_KEY is not set
- Server is otherwise stable and functional

## Hardware/Resource Info
```
Container stats before fix:
NAME           CPU %     MEM USAGE / LIMIT
letta-server   101.87%   1.447GiB / 43.35GiB

Container stats after removing GEMINI key:
NAME           CPU %     MEM USAGE / LIMIT  
letta-server   0.27%     379MiB / 43.35GiB
```

## Severity
**High** - Prevents use of Gemini embeddings and causes severe performance degradation

## Reporter
Environment: Docker deployment, letta-chat-app-deploy repository

Title: 🐛 Bug: Server fails to start with KeyError: '$ref' (FastAPI 0.121.0)
Creator: Duzafizzl
Body:
### 🐛 **Bug: Server fails to start with `KeyError: '$ref'` (FastAPI 0.121.0)**

**Environment:**
- **Letta Version:** 0.13.0
- **FastAPI Version:** 0.121.0 (latest)
- **Pydantic Version:** 2.12.4
- **Python Version:** 3.11
- **OS:** macOS 14.6 / Debian (Raspberry Pi)

---

### **Problem Description**
When starting the Letta server with `letta server`, it crashes during OpenAPI schema generation:

```
KeyError: '$ref'
  File "venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/fastapi/_compat/v2.py", line 310
    old_name = schema["$ref"].split("/")[-1]
               ~~~~~~^^^^^^^^
```

**Impact:** 🔴 **Critical** - Server cannot start, blocking all usage.

---

### **Root Cause**
This is a bug in **FastAPI 0.121.0**'s Pydantic v2 compatibility layer (`fastapi/_compat/v2.py`). 

The function `_remap_definitions_and_field_mappings()` assumes all schemas in `field_mapping` contain a `$ref` key, but some schemas don't have this key, causing a `KeyError`.

---

### **Workaround (Tested & Verified)**

**Option 1: Patch FastAPI** *(Recommended for production)*

Edit: `venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages/fastapi/_compat/v2.py`

**Around line 310**, replace:
```python
        old_name = schema["$ref"].split("/")[-1]

curl http://localhost:8283/v1/health/

```

```

Or add a startup monkey-patch in `letta/server/rest_api/app.py`:

Title: Use Valkey as an Alternative for Redis Caching in docker-compose.yml
Creator: tokiwadai
Body:
## Summary

Adopt Valkey as an alternative to Redis in the development docker-compose configuration, providing a modern, open-source caching solution while maintaining full compatibility.

## Motivation

- **Licensing benefits**: Valkey is a Linux Foundation project fork of Redis with a more permissive license
- **Full compatibility**: Valkey is 100% Redis protocol-compatible, requiring no code changes
- **Active development**: Backed by major tech companies and actively maintained
- **Drop-in compatible**: Uses the same commands, protocols, and client libraries

## Proposed Changes

Update `scripts/docker-compose.yml` to use Valkey as an alternative caching solution:

### Changes Made

```yaml
services:
  redis:
    image: valkey/valkey:alpine          # Changed from redis:alpine
    container_name: valkey               # Changed from redis
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'valkey-cli ping | grep PONG']  # Changed from redis-cli
      interval: 1s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 5
    ports:
      - '6379:6379'
    volumes:
      - ./data/valkey:/data              # Changed from ./data/redis
    command: valkey-server --appendonly yes  # Changed from redis-server
```

### What Changed

| Component | Before (Redis) | After (Valkey) |
|-----------|---------------|----------------|
| Docker image | `redis:alpine` | `valkey/valkey:alpine` |
| Container name | `redis` | `valkey` |
| CLI command | `redis-cli` | `valkey-cli` |
| Server command | `redis-server` | `valkey-server` |
| Data volume | `./data/redis` | `./data/valkey` |

### What Stayed the Same

- Port: `6379` (Redis-compatible)
- All Redis protocols and commands
- Client library compatibility
- Appendonly persistence mode
- Health check mechanism

Title: Fix OpenAI API Key Configuration in .env File
Creator: actuallyrizzn
Body:
## Issue: OpenAI API Key Configuration in .env File

### Problem
When setting up the Letta server via the installer, the `.env` file may be created with quoted values for API keys. This causes the server to fail when attempting to use OpenAI API keys, resulting in 500 errors when creating agents.

### Root Causes

1. **Quoted Environment Variables**
   - Docker's `--env-file` flag includes quotes as part of the environment variable value
   - If `.env` contains: `OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."`
   - Docker sets: `OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."` (with quotes in the value)
   - This causes OpenAI API to reject requests with "Invalid authorization header"

2. **Missing LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY**
   - Letta's Secret class requires `LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to be set, even if encryption is not actively used
   - Without it, the Secret class may incorrectly identify API keys as encrypted and fail to decrypt them
   - This results in `None` being returned instead of the actual API key

### Required Fixes

1. **Ensure .env file format does not include quotes around values:**
   ```bash
   # ✅ Correct
   OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-abc123...
   
   # ❌ Incorrect
   OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-abc123..."
   ```

2. **Ensure LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set in .env:**
   ```bash
   LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY=dummy-encryption-key-32-chars-long!!
   ```
   Note: This is required even if encryption is not being used.

### Impact
- **Severity:** High
- **User Impact:** Server cannot authenticate with OpenAI API, agent creation fails
- **Workaround:** Manual editing of .env file after installation

### References
See detailed incident report for full technical details and investigation.

[1] actuallyrizzn (2025-11-19T16:57:52Z):
# Incident Report: OpenAI API Key Not Being Loaded by Letta Server

**Date:** November 19, 2025  
**Severity:** High  
**Status:** Resolved  
**Affected System:** Letta Server (Self-hosted Docker container)

---

## Executive Summary

The Letta server running in a Docker container was unable to use the OpenAI API key configured in the `.env` file, resulting in 500 Internal Server Error responses when attempting to create agents. The issue was caused by two separate problems:

1. **Quoted API key in .env file** - Docker's `--env-file` was including literal quotes as part of the environment variable value
2. **Secret encryption false positive** - Letta's Secret class incorrectly identified the API key as encrypted, causing decryption to fail and return `None`

Both issues have been resolved, and the server is now functioning correctly.

---

## Problem Description

### Symptoms
- Letta server running in Docker container (screen session)
- Server unable to authenticate with OpenAI API
- HTTP 500 Internal Server Error when creating agents
- Error logs showing: `401 Unauthorized` from OpenAI API
- Error message: `Invalid authorization header`

### Impact
- **User Impact:** Unable to create new agents or use OpenAI-powered features
- **System Impact:** All agent creation requests failing
- **Duration:** Unknown (discovered during troubleshooting session)

---

## Investigation Timeline

### Initial Investigation
1. **Environment Variable Check**
   - Verified `.env` file exists at `/root/.letta/.env`
   - Confirmed `OPENAI_API_KEY` is set in the file
   - Checked Docker container environment variables
   - **Finding:** API key was present but included literal quotes: `"sk-proj-..."`

2. **Docker Container Inspection**
   ```bash
   docker exec <container> printenv OPENAI_API_KEY
   # Output: "sk-proj-..." (with quotes)
   ```
   - **Finding:** Environment variable contained quotes as part of the value

3. **API Key Validation**
   - Tested API key directly with OpenAI Python client
   - **Result:** Key works correctly when used directly
   - **Conclusion:** Key itself is valid; issue is with how it's being passed to OpenAI

### Root Cause Analysis

#### Issue #1: Quoted Environment Variable
**Location:** `/root/.letta/.env`

**Problem:**
```bash
OPENAI_API_KEY="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"
```

Docker's `--env-file` flag does not strip quotes from values. When the `.env` file contains:
```
OPENAI_API_KEY="value"
```

Docker includes the quotes as part of the environment variable value, resulting in:
```
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-..."
```

When this value is used in the Authorization header as `Bearer "sk-proj-..."`, OpenAI rejects it with "Invalid authorization header".

**Fix Applied:**
Removed quotes from the `.env` file:
```bash
sed -i 's/^OPENAI_API_KEY="\(.*\)"$/OPENAI_API_KEY=\1/' /root/.letta/.env
```

**Result:** Environment variable now contains the key without quotes, but issue persisted.

#### Issue #2: Secret Encryption False Positive
**Location:** Letta's Secret class (`/app/letta/schemas/secret.py`)

**Problem:**
After fixing the quotes issue, the API key was still not working. Investigation revealed:

1. Letta uses a `Secret` class to handle API keys
2. The `Secret.from_db()` method calls `Secret.from_plaintext()`
3. `from_plaintext()` checks if the value appears encrypted using `CryptoUtils.is_encrypted()`
4. The OpenAI API key (164 characters, base64-decodable) matched the encryption format pattern
5. `is_encrypted()` returned `True` (false positive)
6. `get_plaintext()` attempted to decrypt the value
7. Without `LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` set, decryption failed
8. Method returned `None` instead of the plaintext key

**Code Flow:**
```python
# Provider creation
provider = OpenAIProvider(
    api_key=model_settings.openai_api_key,  # Key is set correctly
    ...
)

# When making API call
secret = provider.get_api_key_secret()  # Returns Secret object
api_key = secret.get_plaintext()  # Returns None!
```

**Root Cause:**
The `CryptoUtils.is_encrypted()` method uses a heuristic check:
```python
def is_encrypted(cls, value: str) -> bool:
    try:
        decoded = base64.b64decode(value)
        # Check if length matches encryption format
        return len(decoded) >= SALT_SIZE + IV_SIZE + TAG_SIZE + 1
    except Exception:
        return False
```

OpenAI API keys are:
- Base64-decodable (or appear to be)
- Long enough to match the minimum encrypted size (164 characters)
- Therefore incorrectly identified as encrypted

**Fix Applied:**
Added `LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to the `.env` file:
```bash
LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY=dummy-encryption-key-32-chars-long!!
```

**Why This Works:**
- Setting `LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` makes `CryptoUtils.is_encryption_available()` return `True`
- This prevents the `_plaintext_cache` from being cleared in `get_plaintext()`
- The cache set during `from_plaintext()` is preserved and returned correctly

---

## Resolution Steps

### Step 1: Remove Quotes from .env File
```bash
# Edit /root/.letta/.env
sed -i 's/^OPENAI_API_KEY="\(.*\)"$/OPENAI_API_KEY=\1/' /root/.letta/.env

# Verify
cat /root/.letta/.env | grep OPENAI_API_KEY
# Output: OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-... (no quotes)
```

### Step 2: Add LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY
```bash
# Add to /root/.letta/.env
echo "" >> /root/.letta/.env
echo "# Encryption key for Letta secrets (required even if not using encryption)" >> /root/.letta/.env
echo "LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY=dummy-encryption-key-32-chars-long!!" >> /root/.letta/.env
```

### Step 3: Restart Letta Server
```bash
# Stop existing container
docker stop $(docker ps -q --filter ancestor=letta/letta:latest)

# Restart using startup script
bash /root/launch_letta.sh
```

### Step 4: Verification
```bash
# Test Secret.get_plaintext() returns correct value
docker exec <container> python3 -c "
from letta.schemas.providers.openai import OpenAIProvider
from letta.settings import model_settings
from letta.schemas.secret import CryptoUtils

print('Encryption available:', CryptoUtils.is_encryption_available())
provider = OpenAIProvider(name='openai', api_key=model_settings.openai_api_key, base_url='https://api.openai.com/v1')
secret = provider.get_api_key_secret()
plaintext = secret.get_plaintext()
print('Plaintext from secret:', repr(plaintext[:30]) if plaintext else 'None')
"
# Expected output: Plaintext from secret: 'sk-proj-M_WPWcmsG7t-BI_W6qpymR'
```

---

## Technical Details

### Environment Configuration
- **Server:** Self-hosted Letta server in Docker
- **Container:** `letta/letta:latest`
- **Port:** 8284 (host) -> 8283 (container)
- **Environment File:** `/root/.letta/.env`
- **Startup Script:** `/root/launch_letta.sh`

### Files Modified
1. `/root/.letta/.env`
   - Removed quotes from `OPENAI_API_KEY`
   - Added `LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY`

### Code Locations
- **Secret Class:** `/app/letta/schemas/secret.py`
- **Crypto Utils:** `/app/letta/helpers/crypto_utils.py`
- **Provider Class:** `/app/letta/schemas/providers/base.py`
- **OpenAI Provider:** `/app/letta/schemas/providers/openai.py`

### Key Functions Involved
- `Secret.from_db()` - Creates Secret from database values
- `Secret.from_plaintext()` - Creates Secret from plaintext value
- `Secret.get_plaintext()` - Retrieves decrypted plaintext
- `CryptoUtils.is_encrypted()` - Heuristic check for encrypted values
- `CryptoUtils.is_encryption_available()` - Checks if encryption key is configured

---

## Prevention & Recommendations

### Immediate Actions
1. ✅ **Documented .env file format requirements**
   - Do not use quotes around values in `.env` files when using Docker's `--env-file`
   - Docker includes quotes as part of the value

2. ✅ **Added LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY to .env**
   - Required for Secret class to function correctly
   - Even if encryption is not actively used

### Long-term Recommendations

1. **Improve Secret Class Logic**
   - Consider improving `is_encrypted()` heuristic to reduce false positives
   - Add explicit flag to indicate whether a value is actually encrypted
   - Consider storing encryption metadata separately

2. **Environment Variable Validation**
   - Add startup validation to check API keys are properly formatted
   - Log warnings when Secret.get_plaintext() returns None
   - Provide clearer error messages when API authentication fails

3. **Documentation Updates**
   - Document that `LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is required for self-hosted deployments
   - Add examples of correct `.env` file format
   - Document the Secret class behavior and requirements

4. **Testing**
   - Add integration tests for API key loading
   - Test with various API key formats
   - Test Secret class with and without encryption key

### Configuration Best Practices

**Correct .env Format:**
```bash
# ✅ Correct - No quotes
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-proj-abc123...
LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY=dummy-encryption-key-32-chars-long!!
LETTA_SERVER_PASSWORD=go0dp4ssw0rd

# ❌ Incorrect - Quotes included in value
OPENAI_API_KEY="sk-proj-abc123..."
```

**Docker Command:**
```bash
docker run \
  -v ~/.letta/.persist/pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data \
  -p 8284:8283 \
  --env-file ~/.letta/.env \
  -e SECURE=true \
  -e LETTA_SERVER_PASSWORD="go0dp4ssw0rd" \
  --add-host=host.docker.internal:host-gateway \
  letta/letta:latest
```

---

## Lessons Learned

1. **Docker --env-file Behavior**
   - Docker's `--env-file` does not strip quotes from values
   - This is different from shell variable expansion
   - Always verify environment variables in the container

2. **Heuristic Checks Can Fail**
   - The `is_encrypted()` check is a heuristic, not definitive
   - Long, base64-decodable strings can trigger false positives
   - Need explicit metadata or better heuristics

3. **Silent Failures**
   - `Secret.get_plaintext()` returning `None` was a silent failure
   - No clear error message indicated the root cause
   - Better error handling and logging needed

4. **Configuration Requirements**
   - `LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is required even if not using encryption
   - This should be documented and validated at startup

---

## Verification

### Test Results
- ✅ API key correctly loaded in container environment
- ✅ `Secret.get_plaintext()` returns correct value
- ✅ Agent creation succeeds
- ✅ OpenAI API calls work correctly
- ✅ Streaming responses functional

### Monitoring
- Monitor server logs for any Secret-related warnings
- Watch for 401/403 errors from OpenAI API
- Verify agent creation success rate

---

## References

- Letta Server Documentation
- Docker `--env-file` documentation
- Letta Secret class implementation
- OpenAI API authentication requirements

---

## Incident Timeline

| Time | Event |
|------|-------|
| T+0 | Issue reported: Server not picking up OpenAI API key |
| T+5 | Initial investigation: Found quotes in .env file |
| T+10 | Fixed quotes issue, restarted server |
| T+15 | Issue persisted, deeper investigation |
| T+30 | Discovered Secret class false positive |
| T+35 | Added LETTA_ENCRYPTION_KEY to .env |
| T+40 | Restarted server, verified fix |
| T+45 | Incident resolved |

---

**Reviewed By:** [Pending]  
**Date:** November 19, 2025

[1] carenthomas (2025-12-01T19:03:13Z):
Thanks for reporting this issue! The underlying root cause is that the `add_default_initial_messages` flag was defined as a query parameter, which was incorrect. In order to better follow REST API conventions, in the 1.0.0 release of the sdk we have corrected this endpoint to take in a request body, since it is a PATCH request, not a GET request.

As a concrete example, this is what worked before:

```
client.patch(f"/v1/agents/{agent_id}/reset-messages?add_default_initial_messages=true")
```

This is the correct request following REST API conventions:

```
client.patch(
    f"/v1/agents/{agent_id}/reset-messages",
    json={"add_default_initial_messages": True}
)
```

To fix, upgrading to the latest version of the OSS (`0.15.0+`) or latest sdk client (`1.0.0+`) will mitigate the issue!

Title: _parse_function_from_source() evaluates default parameter expressions using bare eval()
Creator: wsargent
Body:
**Describe the bug**

Letta's tool schema generator fails to parse function signatures that use module-level constants as default parameter values. When creating a tool with `client.tools.create(source_code=...)`, if the function uses constants like `DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID` as default parameters, Letta raises:

```
ValueError: Failed to derive json schema: Schema generation failed: non-default argument follows default argument
```

**Root Cause:** In `letta/functions/functions.py`, the `_parse_function_from_source()` function attempts to evaluate default parameter expressions using `eval()` without providing the proper namespace. When it encounters constant references like `DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID`, the `eval()` fails with a `NameError`. Letta then incorrectly creates a parameter **without a default value**, even though the source code has one. This creates an invalid Python signature like `(user_id=None, calendar_id, max_results)` where a parameter with a default is followed by parameters without defaults.

**Please describe your setup**

- [x] How are you running Letta?
  - Docker
- [x] Describe your setup
  - OS: macOS (Darwin 25.1.0)
  - Docker command: Running via `docker compose` with image `letta/letta:0.14.0`
  - Python version in container: 3.11

**Reproduction**

### Minimal Example

This tool definition **FAILS**:

```python
from letta import create_client

source_code = """
from typing import Optional

DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID = "primary"
DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS = 50

def search_calendars(
    user_id: Optional[str] = None,
    calendar_id: str = DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID,
    max_results: int = DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS,
) -> str:
    '''Searches calendar events.'''
    return "test"
"""

client = create_client()
tool = client.tools.create(source_code=source_code)
# ValueError: Failed to derive json schema: Schema generation failed: non-default argument follows default argument
```

### What Happens Internally

1. Parser extracts AST for `search_calendars` function
2. For `user_id = None`: successfully evaluates `None` → creates `Parameter(user_id, default=None)` ✓
3. For `calendar_id = DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID`:
   - Tries `eval("DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID")` without namespace
   - Gets `NameError: name 'DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID' is not defined`
   - **Falls back to creating parameter WITHOUT default**: `Parameter(calendar_id)` ✗
4. For `max_results = DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS`: same failure ✗
5. Attempts to create `Signature([user_id=None, calendar_id, max_results])`
6. Python's `inspect.Signature()` raises: `ValueError: non-default argument follows default argument`

### Test to Verify the Bug

Run this inside the Letta container to reproduce the exact parsing issue:

```python
import inspect
import ast

source_code = """
DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID = "primary"
DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS = 50

def search_calendars(
    user_id: Optional[str] = None,
    calendar_id: str = DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID,
    max_results: int = DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS,
) -> str:
    return "test"
"""

tree = ast.parse(source_code)
func_def = None
for node in ast.walk(tree):
    if isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == "search_calendars":
        func_def = node
        break

parameters = []
num_args = len(func_def.args.args)
num_defaults = len(func_def.args.defaults)
num_required = num_args - num_defaults

for i, arg in enumerate(func_def.args.args):
    default_index = i - num_required
    if default_index >= 0:
        default_value = func_def.args.defaults[default_index]
        default_expr = ast.unparse(default_value)
        try:
            # This is what Letta does - eval without namespace
            evaluated = eval(default_expr)
            param = inspect.Parameter(arg.arg, inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD, default=evaluated)
        except NameError as e:
            # When eval fails, creates param WITHOUT default (BUG!)
            print(f"ERROR: {arg.arg} = {default_expr} failed: {e}")
            param = inspect.Parameter(arg.arg, inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD)
    else:
        param = inspect.Parameter(arg.arg, inspect.Parameter.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD)
    parameters.append(param)

# This will fail
sig = inspect.Signature(parameters)
# ValueError: non-default argument follows default argument
```

**Expected Behavior**

The tool schema generator should successfully parse functions with constant references as default parameters. It should either:
1. Evaluate defaults with the proper namespace (including module-level constants), OR
2. Preserve the constant reference in the default value, OR
3. Recognize that the parameter has a default even if it can't be evaluated

**Workaround**

Inline all constant values directly in the function signature:

```python
# WORKS - inline the constants
def search_calendars(
    user_id: Optional[str] = None,
    calendar_id: str = "primary",  # Inlined instead of DEFAULT_CALENDAR_ID
    max_results: int = 50,         # Inlined instead of DEFAULT_MAX_RESULTS
) -> str:
    '''Searches calendar events.'''
    return "test"
```

**Screenshots**

Error from Letta logs:
```
Letta.letta.services.tool_schema_generator - WARNING - Failed to derive json schema: Schema generation failed: non-default argument follows default argument
Letta.letta.server.rest_api.app - ERROR - ValueError
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/app/letta/functions/functions.py", line 300, in derive_openai_json_schema
    mock_func = _parse_function_from_source(source_code, name)
  File "/app/letta/functions/functions.py", line 282, in _parse_function_from_source
    signature = inspect.Signature(parameters)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.11/inspect.py", line 3007, in __init__
    raise ValueError(msg)
ValueError: non-default argument follows default argument
```

**Additional context**

- **Letta version**: 0.14.0
- **Models**: Claude Sonnet 4 (Anthropic), Gemini 2.0 Flash (Google) - both via API
- **Impact**: This bug prevents users from following Python best practices (DRY principle with constants) and creating maintainable tool definitions with centralized configuration

**Files Affected**
- `/app/letta/functions/functions.py` - `_parse_function_from_source()`
- `/app/letta/services/tool_schema_generator.py` - `generate_schema_for_tool_creation()`

**Suggested Fix**

In `letta/functions/functions.py`, when evaluating default parameter values:

1. **Option 1**: Execute the entire source code to populate a namespace, then evaluate defaults within that namespace
2. **Option 2**: When `eval()` fails with `NameError`, still recognize that the parameter has a default and use a sentinel value or the unparsed AST expression
3. **Option 3**: Use `ast.literal_eval()` where possible, and for non-literal defaults (like constant references), preserve them as-is without requiring evaluation

# Line 30: embedding is defined as a string
class ArchiveCreateRequest(BaseModel):
    embedding: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Embedding model handle for the archive")

# Lines 67-68: Code incorrectly treats it as an object
if embedding_config is None and archive.embedding is not None:
    handle = f"{archive.embedding.provider}/{archive.embedding.model}"  # ❌ Bug!
```

The `embedding` field is defined as `Optional[str]` (line 30), but the code on line 68 tries to access `.provider` and `.model` attributes as if it were an object.

**Steps to Reproduce**

Using the Letta Python client:

```python
from letta_client import Letta

client = Letta(base_url="http://localhost:8283", token="your_token")

# This triggers the bug
archive = client.archives.create(
    name="test-archive",
    description="Test archive",
    embedding="letta/letta-free"
)
```

**Expected Behavior**

The archive should be created successfully using the string handle `"letta/letta-free"`.

**Suggested Fix**

Since `archive.embedding` is already a string handle in the format `"provider/model"` (e.g., `"letta/letta-free"`), the code should use it directly:

Change line 68 in `letta/server/rest_api/routers/v1/archives.py` from:
```python
handle = f"{archive.embedding.provider}/{archive.embedding.model}"
```
to:
```python
handle = archive.embedding
```

Full corrected code block (lines 66-72):
```python
embedding_config = archive.embedding_config
if embedding_config is None and archive.embedding is not None:
    handle = archive.embedding  # ✅ Fix: use the string directly
    embedding_config = await server.get_embedding_config_from_handle_async(
        handle=handle,
        actor=actor,
    )
```

Title: Feature Request: Venice AI Provider Integration
Creator: actuallyrizzn
Body:
# Feature Request: Venice AI Provider Integration

## Summary

Add Venice AI as a new LLM provider option in Letta, enabling users to use Venice AI models for chat completions, streaming, tool calling, and embeddings generation.

## Motivation

Venice AI provides access to multiple LLM models through a unified API. Integrating Venice AI as a provider would give Letta users:
- Access to a diverse set of models through a single provider
- OpenAI-compatible API format for seamless integration
- Dynamic model discovery (models listed from API, not hardcoded)
- Support for chat completions, streaming, tool calling, and embeddings

## Proposed Solution

Implement a Venice AI provider that:
1. Extends `LLMClientBase` following Letta's existing provider patterns
2. Supports all core LLM operations (chat, streaming, embeddings, tool calling)
3. Dynamically lists available models from Venice API
4. Handles errors and retries appropriately
5. Maintains 100% test coverage

## Benefits

- **More Model Options**: Users gain access to Venice AI's model catalog
- **Unified Interface**: Works seamlessly with Letta's existing agent and LLM infrastructure
- **OpenAI-Compatible**: Venice uses OpenAI-compatible format, making integration straightforward
- **Dynamic Discovery**: Models are automatically discovered from API (no hardcoded lists)
- **Full Feature Support**: Chat, streaming, tool calling, and embeddings all supported

## Implementation Details

The implementation would include:
- `VeniceClient`: LLM client extending `LLMClientBase`
- `VeniceProvider`: Provider class for dynamic model listing
- Configuration via `VENICE_API_KEY` environment variable or settings
- Comprehensive test coverage (unit, integration, E2E)
- Full documentation

## Configuration

Users would configure Venice AI by setting:
```bash
export VENICE_API_KEY="your-api-key"
```

Or in settings:
```python
venice_api_key = "your-api-key"
```

Models would be automatically discovered and available as `venice/{model_id}`.

## Additional Context

Venice AI provides an OpenAI-compatible API, which means:
- Request/response formats are already compatible with Letta's OpenAI client patterns
- Streaming uses Server-Sent Events (SSE) format
- Tool calling follows OpenAI function calling format
- Embeddings use OpenAI-compatible endpoint

This makes the integration straightforward and maintainable.

Title: CLI for managing agent fleets
Creator: nouamanecodes
Body:
Hey guys, I've been working on something that I think could be really valuable for the Letta ecosystem.

## What I Built
I created **LettaCTL** - basically kubectl but for Letta agents. Think "Docker Compose for AI agents" where you can define your entire agent setup in YAML and deploy everything with one command.

**Repository**: [here](https://github.com/nouamanecodes/lettactl)

## The Problem
Right now, managing multiple Letta agents is kind of a pain. Every time I want to set up agents for a project, I'm:
- Manually clicking through the UI to create each agent
- Copy-pasting system prompts and losing track of versions
- Recreating the same setup over and over
- Struggling to share agent configurations with teammates
- Having no real way to version control my agent setups

## What LettaCTL Does
Instead of all that manual work, you can now:
- Define agents in YAML files (just like k8s manifests)
- Deploy entire agent fleets with `lettactl apply -f agents.yml`
- Automatically version agents when you change their system prompts or memory blocks (diff-based updates)
- Share memory blocks and tools across multiple agents (also with versioning)
- Auto-discover Python tools and documents with glob patterns
- Send messages and manage conversations from the command line
- Export/import agents for backup and sharing

## Quick Example - Deploy an Entire Agent Fleet
```yaml
# agents.yml
shared_blocks:
  - name: company-knowledge
    description: "Company-wide knowledge base"
    from_file: "shared/company-info.md"
  - name: product-specs
    description: "Product specifications"
    from_file: "shared/product-specs.md"

agents:
  - name: customer-support
    description: "Customer support agent"
    llm_config:
      model: "google_ai/gemini-2.5-pro"
      context_window: 32000
    system_prompt:
      from_file: "prompts/support-agent.md"
    shared_blocks:
      - company-knowledge
      - product-specs
    tools:
      - tools/*  # Auto-discovers all tools

  - name: sales-assistant
    description: "Sales assistant agent"
    llm_config:
      model: "google_ai/gemini-2.5-pro"
      context_window: 32000
    system_prompt:
      from_file: "prompts/sales-agent.md"
    shared_blocks:
      - company-knowledge
      - product-specs
    folders:
      - name: sales-materials
        files:
          - "files/*"  # Auto-discovers all files

  - name: technical-support
    description: "Technical support specialist"
    llm_config:
      model: "google_ai/gemini-2.5-pro"
      context_window: 32000
    system_prompt:
      from_file: "prompts/tech-support.md"
    shared_blocks:
      - product-specs
    tools:
      - tools/debugging_tools/*
```

```bash
# Deploy entire fleet with one command
lettactl apply -f agents.yml

# Now you have 3 specialized agents sharing knowledge bases
lettactl get agents
lettactl send customer-support "Help with billing"
lettactl send sales-assistant "Tell me about the premium plan"
lettactl send technical-support "Debug connection issue"
```

This deploys 3 specialized agents that share knowledge bases and tools - something that would take forever to set up manually and be impossible to keep in sync.

## Auto-Discovery Magic
The real time-saver is the auto-discovery. Just drop files in directories and use glob patterns:

```yaml
agents:
  - name: document-expert
    tools:
      - tools/*           # Auto-discovers ALL Python tools
      - tools/pdf/*       # Just PDF-related tools
    folders:
      - name: docs
        files:
          - "files/*"      # All files in files/ directory
          - "files/**/*"   # Recursively finds everything
          - "manuals/*.pdf" # Just PDFs in manuals/
    shared_blocks:
      - knowledge-base     # Shared across agents
```

Your file structure:
```
project/
├── agents.yml
├── files/
│   ├── manual.pdf
│   ├── specs/
│   │   └── api-docs.md
│   └── guides/
│       └── setup.txt
├── tools/
│   ├── search_tool.py
│   ├── pdf/
│   │   └── pdf_reader.py
│   └── web/
│       └── web_scraper.py
└── shared/
    └── company-knowledge.md
```

LettaCTL automatically finds and attaches everything. No manual file listing needed.

## What Commands Are Available
The basics you'd expect:
- `lettactl apply` - Deploy your agent configurations
- `lettactl get agents` - See what's running
- `lettactl send <agent> <message>` - Chat with agents
- `lettactl messages <agent>` - View conversation history
- `lettactl export/import` - Backup and restore agents

Plus all the CRUD stuff for managing agents, blocks, and resources.


What do you think? Would love to chat about potentially integrating this into the main project or at least making it an official community tool.

---

[1] cpacker (2025-12-04T09:02:41Z):
This is super cool! I need to dive deeper into it - but my first reflex is maybe this makes sense to roll into the Letta CLI here: https://github.com/letta-ai/letta-code ?

It's not really an apples to apples comparison, since the direct usecase is more like local agent vs managing agent fleet, but both are CLIs, and we are starting to add more "agent management" tooling into `letta-code` so I wonder if it'll overlap. Curious what you think!

[2] nouamanecodes (2025-12-05T00:33:51Z):
Yeah there's definitely overlap. I think in order to make it powerful and flexible it would be great to have

1. An easy way to tell any agent, including `letta-code` "Hey build me 20 agents with this yaml config"
2. An easy way to do this from a direct command so that it can be done in CI or within app changes like when you onboard a new user or something (this was my main use case)

What would work well would be to have a new subcommand called `letta fleet` or something which essentially replaces `lettactl`. That way it can work any way someone's workflow needs, and it would separate the code concerns so the `lettactl` code can just be ported right into the codebase (it's just a set of commander commands) easily without making any architecture changes to `letta-code`

If we decide to go this direction then it probably makes sense to remove some of the current `lettactl` commands like `lettactl send <agentname> "message to agent"` since there's already a way to do it with `letta-code`

Title: OpenRouterProvider missing list_embedding_models_async() - embedding models not discovered
Creator: lagiosv
Body:
### Problem

When using OpenRouter as an LLM provider, Letta cannot discover embedding models. The `OpenRouterProvider` class inherits from `OpenAIProvider` but doesn't implement `list_embedding_models_async()`.

**Current behavior:**
- Only `letta/letta-free` embedding model appears in the UI/API
- OpenRouter embedding models (e.g., `openai/text-embedding-3-small`) are not discoverable
- Users cannot create agents with OpenRouter embeddings through normal flows

**Root cause:**
OpenRouter's `/models` endpoint only returns LLM models, not embedding models. Unlike OpenAI's API, there's no `/models` response that includes embedding model metadata.

### Environment
- Letta version: 0.15.1 (Docker)
- Provider: OpenRouter with `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set

### Proposed Solution

Add `list_embedding_models_async()` method to `OpenRouterProvider` class in `letta/schemas/providers/openrouter.py`.

Since OpenRouter doesn't expose embedding models via their API, the solution is to return hardcoded `EmbeddingConfig` objects for the known supported models:

```python
async def list_embedding_models_async(self) -> list[EmbeddingConfig]:
    """
    Return hardcoded OpenRouter embedding models.
    OpenRouter's /models endpoint doesn't list embedding models,
    but they support OpenAI's embedding models via the /embeddings endpoint.
    """
    return [
        EmbeddingConfig(
            embedding_model="openai/text-embedding-3-small",
            embedding_endpoint_type="openai",
            embedding_endpoint=self.base_url,
            embedding_dim=1536,
            embedding_chunk_size=DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_CHUNK_SIZE,
            handle=self.get_handle("openai/text-embedding-3-small", is_embedding=True),
            batch_size=DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE,
        ),
        EmbeddingConfig(
            embedding_model="openai/text-embedding-3-large",
            embedding_endpoint_type="openai",
            embedding_endpoint=self.base_url,
            embedding_dim=3072,
            embedding_chunk_size=DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_CHUNK_SIZE,
            handle=self.get_handle("openai/text-embedding-3-large", is_embedding=True),
            batch_size=DEFAULT_EMBEDDING_BATCH_SIZE,
        ),
    ]
```

### Testing Done

Tested with a patched `openrouter.py` mounted via Docker volume:

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| Embedding models appear in API | ✅ 3 models (letta-free + 2 OpenRouter) |
| Agent creation with `openai/text-embedding-3-small` | ✅ Works |
| Archival memory insert (generates embeddings) | ✅ 1536-dim vectors stored |
| Archival memory search (semantic retrieval) | ✅ Returns ranked results |

### Additional Context

- OpenRouter uses the same `/embeddings` endpoint format as OpenAI
- The `embedding_endpoint_type="openai"` ensures compatibility
- This is a minimal change that unblocks OpenRouter users
- Happy to submit a PR if this approach is acceptable

### Related Issues
- #1670 - OpenRouter API support (closed, general support added)
- #1784 - archival_memory_insert error with OpenRouter (closed, was about API key config)

Title: GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/core-memory/blocks returns duplicate blocks across pages
Creator: BVCampos
Body:
## Describe the bug

The `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/core-memory/blocks` endpoint returns **duplicate blocks when paginating**.  
The same block IDs are returned multiple times across pagination requests, resulting in the client receiving more blocks than actually exist.

### Example

An agent created with **3 memory blocks** (`persona`, `system`, `human`) returns:

- **Total blocks returned:** 6  
- **Unique block IDs:** 3  

#### Block ID counts
- `block-ce930f61-e152-4e98-9a18-315b35581803` — 3 times (`system`)
- `block-22ecddf7-93f5-4f6a-9807-85bf7372a80d` — 2 times (`human`)
- `block-6fec3b2e-002a-443f-8ef0-1469cb143d82` — 1 time (`persona`)

### Server logs

The server shows multiple paginated requests being made:

GET /v1/agents/{id}/core-memory/blocks HTTP/1.1 200 OK
GET /v1/agents/{id}/core-memory/blocks?after=block-3553bfbb-... HTTP/1.1 200 OK
GET /v1/agents/{id}/core-memory/blocks?after=block-65e0062e-... HTTP/1.1 200 OK
GET /v1/agents/{id}/core-memory/blocks?after=block-6fec3b2e-... HTTP/1.1 200 OK


The pagination logic appears to **not properly exclude already-returned blocks**.

> **Note:** Block updates still work correctly (all duplicates point to the same underlying block), so this is primarily a listing/display issue.

---

## Please describe your setup

### How are you running Letta?
- Docker

### Environment
- **OS:** macOS (Darwin 24.5.0)
- **Deployment:** Docker Compose using `letta/letta:latest`
- **Client:** `letta-client` (latest)

---

## Reproduction steps

```python
from letta_client import Letta

client = Letta(base_url="http://localhost:8283")

# Create an agent with memory blocks
agent = client.agents.create(
    name="test-agent",
    model="openai/gpt-4o-mini",
    embedding="openai/text-embedding-ada-002",
    memory_blocks=[
        {"label": "persona", "value": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"label": "system", "value": "System instructions here."},
        {"label": "human", "value": "User context here."},
    ],
)

# List blocks - returns duplicates
blocks = list(client.agents.blocks.list(agent_id=agent.id))
print(f"Total blocks returned: {len(blocks)}")  # Returns 6, expected 3

# Verify duplicates
block_ids = [b.id for b in blocks]
unique_ids = set(block_ids)
print(f"Unique block IDs: {len(unique_ids)}")  # Returns 3

from collections import Counter
for bid, count in Counter(block_ids).items():
    if count > 1:
        print(f"Duplicate: {bid} appears {count} times")
```

## Expected behavior

client.agents.blocks.list() should return each block exactly once.
For this example, the expected result is 3 total blocks.

### Additional context

Model: openai/gpt-4o-mini

Embedding: openai/text-embedding-ada-002

Issue persists with freshly created agents

Deleting and recreating the agent does not resolve the issue
Comments:
[1] actuallyrizzn (2025-12-14T07:38:48Z):
## Fix Summary

I've identified and fixed the duplicate blocks issue in the `GET /v1/agents/{agent_id}/core-memory/blocks` endpoint. The problem was caused by two bugs in the pagination logic within `list_agent_blocks_async` method.

## Root Cause Analysis

### Bug 1: Missing Distinct Clause
The query joins `BlockModel` with `BlocksAgents`, which can produce duplicate rows even with unique constraints. The query was missing a `.distinct()` clause to ensure each block appears only once in the result set.

### Bug 2: Incorrect Pagination Cursor Logic
The pagination cursor logic didn't account for the `ascending` parameter. When using cursor-based pagination:
- **Ascending order**: `after=cursor` should return blocks with `id > cursor` (larger IDs come after)
- **Descending order**: `after=cursor` should return blocks with `id < cursor` (smaller IDs come after in descending order)

The original code always used `id > after` regardless of sort order, causing blocks to be incorrectly included/excluded across pages.

## Fix Applied

### File: `letta/services/agent_manager.py`

**Changes made to `list_agent_blocks_async` method (lines 2930-2948):**

1. **Added distinct clause** to prevent duplicate blocks:
   ```python
   .distinct(BlockModel.id)  # Ensure we don't get duplicate blocks by ID
   ```
   Note: Using `distinct(BlockModel.id)` instead of `.distinct()` to avoid PostgreSQL errors with JSON column comparisons.

2. **Fixed pagination cursor logic** to respect ascending/descending order:
   ```python
   # Apply cursor-based pagination
   if before:
       if ascending:
           query = query.where(BlockModel.id < before)
       else:
           query = query.where(BlockModel.id > before)
   if after:
       if ascending:
           query = query.where(BlockModel.id > after)
       else:
           query = query.where(BlockModel.id < after)
   ```

## Code Changes

```python
# Before (lines 2930-2942):
query = (
    select(BlockModel)
    .join(BlocksAgents, BlockModel.id == BlocksAgents.block_id)
    .where(BlocksAgents.agent_id == agent_id, BlockModel.organization_id == actor.organization_id)
)

# Apply cursor-based pagination
if before:
    query = query.where(BlockModel.id < before)
if after:
    query = query.where(BlockModel.id > after)

# After (lines 2930-2948):
query = (
    select(BlockModel)
    .join(BlocksAgents, BlockModel.id == BlocksAgents.block_id)
    .where(BlocksAgents.agent_id == agent_id, BlockModel.organization_id == actor.organization_id)
    .distinct(BlockModel.id)  # Ensure we don't get duplicate blocks by ID
)

# Apply cursor-based pagination
if before:
    if ascending:
        query = query.where(BlockModel.id < before)
    else:
        query = query.where(BlockModel.id > before)
if after:
    if ascending:
        query = query.where(BlockModel.id > after)
    else:
        query = query.where(BlockModel.id < after)
```

## Test Verification

I've created a test case `test_list_agent_blocks_pagination_no_duplicates` in `tests/test_client.py` that:

1. Creates an agent with 3 memory blocks (persona, system, human)
2. Paginates through blocks with `limit=1` to force multiple pages
3. Collects all blocks across pages using the `after` cursor
4. Verifies:
   - Exactly 3 unique blocks are returned (not 6)
   - No duplicate block IDs
   - All expected labels are present

**Test Result**: ✅ **PASSED**

The test successfully verifies that:
- With the fix: Returns exactly 3 unique blocks
- Without the fix: Would return 6 blocks (duplicates)

## Verification Steps

To verify the fix works:

```python
from letta_client import Letta

client = Letta(base_url="http://localhost:8283")

# Create an agent with memory blocks
agent = client.agents.create(
    name="test-agent",
    model="openai/gpt-4o-mini",
    embedding="openai/text-embedding-ada-002",
    memory_blocks=[
        {"label": "persona", "value": "You are a helpful assistant."},
        {"label": "system", "value": "System instructions here."},
        {"label": "human", "value": "User context here."},
    ],
)

# List blocks - should return exactly 3 unique blocks
blocks = list(client.agents.blocks.list(agent_id=agent.id))
print(f"Total blocks returned: {len(blocks)}")  # Should be 3

# Verify no duplicates
block_ids = [b.id for b in blocks]
unique_ids = set(block_ids)
print(f"Unique block IDs: {len(unique_ids)}")  # Should be 3
assert len(blocks) == len(unique_ids), "Duplicate blocks detected!"
```

## Related Code Patterns

This fix follows the same pattern used in other similar methods in the codebase:
- `list_agent_tags_async` (line 3127) - uses `.distinct()` for tag pagination
- `list_agent_sources_async` (line 1766) - uses `.distinct()` for source pagination
- `block_manager.py` (lines 336-338) - uses `distinct(BlockModel.id)` for block queries

## Impact

- ✅ Fixes duplicate blocks when paginating
- ✅ Maintains backward compatibility
- ✅ No breaking changes to API
- ✅ Follows existing codebase patterns

The fix is ready for review and testing.

Title: Feature Request: Qwen Provider Integration
Creator: xiziqijoke
Body:
Summary
Add Qwen (Alibaba Cloud's large language model) as a new LLM provider option in Letta, enabling users to use Qwen series models for chat completions, streaming, tool calling, and embeddings generation.

Motivation

Qwen provides access to a series of high-performance LLM models (including Qwen-2, Qwen-1.5, etc.) through a unified and standardized API. Integrating Qwen as a provider would give Letta users:

- Access to a diverse set of high-quality, Chinese-optimized models through a single provider

- Standardized API format that aligns with industry common practices for seamless integration

- Dynamic model discovery (models listed from Qwen API, not hardcoded), adapting to new model releases in real-time

- Comprehensive support for core LLM capabilities: chat completions, streaming, tool calling, and embeddings generation

Proposed Solution

Implement a Qwen provider that:

- Extends Letta's existing LLMClientBase following the established provider patterns

- Supports all core LLM operations: chat completions, streaming responses, embeddings generation, and tool calling

- Dynamically fetches and lists available Qwen models from the official Qwen API

- Implements robust error handling and retry mechanisms for API stability

- Maintains 100% test coverage (unit, integration, and E2E tests)

Benefits

- Rich Model Ecosystem: Users gain access to Qwen's full model catalog, including general-purpose models, specialized models, and different parameter scales (e.g., Qwen-2-7B, Qwen-2-72B, Qwen-1.5-Chat)

- Seamless Integration: Aligns with Letta's existing agent and LLM infrastructure, requiring no major adjustments to user workflows

- Chinese-Optimized Support: Qwen models have excellent performance in Chinese language understanding and generation, expanding Letta's applicability in Chinese-speaking scenarios

- Dynamic Model Discovery: Automatically synchronizes new Qwen models via API, eliminating the need for manual code updates to add new models

- Full Feature Parity: Supports all core capabilities required by Letta, including streaming and tool calling, ensuring a consistent user experience across providers

Implementation Details

The implementation would include:

- QwenClient: An LLM client class extending LLMClientBase, responsible for interacting with Qwen's API

- QwenProvider: A provider class for dynamic model listing and provider registration

- Configuration support via environment variables or Letta's settings file (for API key management)

- Comprehensive test coverage: unit tests for client logic, integration tests for API interaction, and E2E tests for end-to-end user workflows

- Detailed documentation: configuration guide, supported models list, and usage examples

Configuration

Users would configure Qwen by setting the API key via environment variable or Letta's settings:

Via environment variable:

export QWEN_API_KEY="your-api-key"

Or in Letta's settings:

qwen_api_key = "your-api-key"

Models would be automatically discovered and available in the formatqwen/{model_id} (e.g., qwen/qwen-2-7b-chat, qwen/qwen-1.5-14b-chat).

Additional Context

Qwen provides a standardized RESTful API that supports industry-common request/response formats, which means:

- Chat completion and tool calling request/response formats are compatible with Letta's existing adapter patterns

- Streaming responses use Server-Sent Events (SSE) format, consistent with Letta's existing streaming handling logic

- Embeddings generation uses a dedicated, easy-to-integrate endpoint with clear input/output specifications

These characteristics make the integration of Qwen straightforward, low-cost, and maintainable for future iterations.

Thank you!

Title: Sleeptime message grouping causes role confusion
Creator: temujin9
Body:
**Describe the bug**
Sleeptime trigger evaluates after each capture call, not after a complete request/response cycle is finished. There's no atomicity guarantee that all parts of a multi-part assistant response are processed together before sleeptime evaluation.

1. Frontend sends multi-part assistant response (e.g., thinking block + response text) via /messages/capture
2. Each part creates a separate Message in Letta
3. Sleeptime frequency counter increments per message batch
4. If counter hits trigger threshold between assistant message parts, sleeptime fires mid-response
5. Sleeptime agent receives incomplete context: thinking block without response text, or response without full conversation
6. Missing context causes sleeptime to misinterpret its role - attempts conversational response instead of memory processing.

**Please describe your setup**
- [x] How are you running Letta?
  - Using Letta Cloud, but this bug is visible in OSS version as well.
- [x] Describe your setup
  - Linux, accessing Letta Cloud api via custom rust and letta-python.

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.
- I'm using Opus with very fresh context window (freshly created agents) in sleeptime.
- I can semi-reliably reproduce this both on first turn sleeptime (another oddity, for another bug report) and further in.

**Agent File (optional)**
Please attach your `.af` file, as this helps with reproducing issues.
Comments:
[1] temujin9 (2025-12-17T20:22:07Z):
I can implement a fix for this repo (which would presumably land in Letta Cloud). To do so, either a) letta stop honoring the number of turns for sleeptime so precisely, or b) we change what a turn means in a way that expands how much each one contains (1 user request + all responses).

[2] temujin9 (2025-12-17T20:30:34Z):
I don't have an agent file showing the issue, as I already deleted the agent, but I do have one showing a workaround / fix: grouping all agent responses before submitting. This was hackily done with a custom client, and would need a different approach natively.

[test - Sleeptime.af.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24221234/test.-.Sleeptime.af.json)

(PS - Github doesn't like .af extension, I had to add the .json to get it to upload. You might want to reconsider filename formats, if you want people to upload the results.)

[3] carenthomas (2025-12-17T22:21:23Z):
Thanks for starting the discussion! The `/messages/capture` endpoint is experimental right now, and agree that the current sleeptime abstraction isn't the most ideal for it. I'm actively thinking about what might be a better way for sleeptime to ingest this data.

I'm surprised it performs so poorly, given that the previous messages should still be passed into the history, to gain a more complete understanding on follow-up turns. I'll tune the prompting here, but agree that it's better for sleeptime to get it right the first time rather than having to backtrack.

> a) letta stop honoring the number of turns for sleeptime so precisely

I think this might be complicated to implement dynamically, because the nature of sleeptime is that it runs in the background rather than based on a specific trigger. The main way to implement it would be to rely on sleeptime to decline processing if it seems like the assistant is mid turn. Would achieve the dynamic aspect, but could be costly in terms of additional inference.

A naive solution might be to increase the default frequency for the capture endpoint (and add additional prompting) to maximize the change that a set of messages includes a full turn. Would love to see some examples if you have it available to see what low hanging fruit there might be in the immediate term.

> b) we change what a turn means in a way that expands how much each one contains (1 user request + all responses).

In this case, are you dropping the remaining interleaved user messages and only keeping the first one? Or are you keeping all of the messages, but grouping all the user messages and assistant responses together respectively? Also curious what your use case is - coding, or something else?

[4] temujin9 (2025-12-17T23:32:22Z):
Unfortunately, that naive solution won't work reliably: I've seen reproduction on a cleave in the middle of much later context. Sadly, I didn't save that particular failure, it was instructive. Prompt tuning alone probably won't help: I tried several attempts at that first, though I may not be as good at it.

For (b), I was proposing keeping all messages, grouping user message with all subsequent assistant responses, and submitting only after the next user message comes in, to clearly delimit the end of the prior batch. (It's what I'm doing for my current backfill on the capture endpoint, and it seems to work without issue.) That would make five turns "five user messages and all agent responses to that", which seems logical enough to explain in documentation.

Title: Intermittent streaming failure with Ollama - tools fail to execute with "Received 0 events"
Creator: shaunmorris
Body:
## Bug Description
Tool execution fails intermittently when using Ollama models with Letta v0.16.1. The same tool call sometimes executes successfully, other times fails silently with the streaming parser receiving zero events.

## Environment
- **Letta Version**: v0.16.1 (Docker)
- **Setup**: Letta Docker container + Ollama on host
- **Ollama Version**: Latest (accessed via http://host.docker.internal:11434)
- **Model**: llama3.1:8b
- **Tools**: fetch_webpage, web_search (EXA_API_KEY configured)
- **Failure Rate**: ~30-50% of requests

## Expected Behavior
Tool calls should execute consistently every time.

## Actual Behavior
**Sometimes (50-70% of time):**
- Tool call executes properly
- Agent receives and describes results
- Works as expected

**Other times (30-50% of time):**
- Tool call JSON displayed as text message
- No tool execution occurs
- Logs show: `Received 0 events, last event: None`

## Reproduction Steps
1. Set up Letta Docker with Ollama backend
2. Create agent with llama3.1:8b and utility tools enabled
3. Send multiple requests like: "Please fetch https://example.com"
4. Observe intermittent failures

## Logs
When failure occurs:
httpx - INFO - HTTP Request: POST http://host.docker.internal:11434/v1/chat/completions "HTTP/1.1 200 OK"
Letta.letta.interfaces.openai_streaming_interface - INFO - Chat Completions stream iterator exited (SimpleOpenAIStreamingInterface). Received 0 events, last event: None
Letta.letta.interfaces.openai_streaming_interface - INFO - SimpleOpenAIStreamingInterface: Stream processing complete. Received 0 events, last event: None, stream was cancelled: False


## Proof Ollama Works Correctly
Direct curl test to Ollama shows it ALWAYS returns proper streaming events:

```bash
curl -N http://localhost:11434/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "llama3.1:8b",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Call test_function"}],
    "stream": true,
    "tools": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "test_function", "description": "Test", "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {}}}}]
  }'

Returns:
data: {"id":"chatcmpl-986","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1766023159,"model":"llama3.1:8b","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"role":"assistant","content":"","tool_calls":[{"id":"call_2aa749ra","index":0,"type":"function","function":{"name":"test_function","arguments":"{}"}}]},"finish_reason":null}]}

data: [DONE]

Analysis

    HTTP requests succeed (200 OK)
    Ollama sends proper streaming events every time
    Letta's SimpleOpenAIStreamingInterface intermittently fails to parse these events
    This makes Ollama unreliable for production use with Letta

Impact

    Cannot rely on tools working consistently
    Degrades user experience
    No workaround available (no option to disable streaming)

Request

Please investigate why the streaming parser fails intermittently despite Ollama returning valid responses every time.
